title.zh: 卷385 列傳一百七十二 杜受田子：翰 祁俊藻子：世长 翁心存 彭蕴章
title.en: Volume 385 Biographies 172: Du Shoutian son: Han, Qi Junzao son: Shi Zhang, Weng Xincun, Peng Yunzhang
title.raw: 卷385 列傳一百七十二 杜受田子：翰 祁俊藻子：世长 翁心存 彭蕴章

sentences.zh: 杜受田，字芝農，山東濱州人。

translations.literal: Du Shoutian, styled Zhinong, was a native of Binzhou, Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shoutian, whose courtesy name was Zhinong, came from Binzhou in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 父堮，嘉慶六年進士，由翰林院編修累官禮部侍郎，重宴鹿鳴，加太子少保，卒贈太傅，諡文端。

translations.literal: His father Fu, a jinshi of the sixth year of Jiaqing, rose from Hanlin Academy compiler to Vice Minister of Rites, attended a second Deer Cry banquet, was elevated to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and upon death was posthumously granted Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fu had passed the metropolitan examination in the sixth year of the Jiaqing reign and advanced from compiler at the Hanlin Academy to vice minister of rites. When he was honored with a second Deer Cry banquet, he received the title of junior guardian of the heir apparent. After his death he was posthumously made grand tutor and given the posthumous name Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 受田，道光三年進士，會試第一，殿試二甲第一，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: Shoutian, a jinshi of the third year of Daoguang, ranked first in the metropolitan examination, first in the second class of the palace examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Shoutian earned his jinshi degree in the third year of the Daoguang reign, placing first in the metropolitan examination and first in the second class of the palace examination. He was chosen as a Hanlin bachelor and appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 大考擢中允，遷洗馬，督山西學政。

translations.literal: In the major examination he was promoted to middle attendant, transferred to groom of the heir apparent, and supervised educational administration in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the triennial palace examination he was promoted to middle attendant, then transferred to groom of the heir apparent, and was appointed educational commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 十五年，特召還京，直上書房，授文宗讀。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was specially summoned back to the capital, entered the Upper Study, and instructed Wenzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of the reign he was specially recalled to the capital, assigned to the Upper Study, and charged with tutoring the future Emperor Wenzong.

sentences.zh: 四遷內閣學士，命專心授讀，毋庸到閣批本。

translations.literal: After four promotions he became a Grand Secretariat academician and was ordered to devote himself solely to instruction, without needing to attend the Secretariat to endorse memorials.
translations.idiomatic: After four further promotions he became a grand secretariat academician and was instructed to devote himself entirely to teaching, exempt from attending the secretariat to endorse memorials.

sentences.zh: 十八年，擢工部侍郎，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works and transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to vice minister of works and transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，連擢左都御史、工部尚書，尋充上書房總師傅。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was successively promoted to Censor-in-Chief of the Left and Minister of Works, and soon thereafter appointed chief tutor of the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was promoted in quick succession to censor-in-chief of the left and minister of works, and soon afterward was made chief tutor of the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 文宗自六歲入學，受田朝夕納誨，必以正道，歷十餘年。

translations.literal: From the age of six when Wenzong entered his studies, Shoutian admonished him morning and evening, always by the upright path, for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Wenzong began his studies at the age of six, Shoutian instructed him morning and evening along the path of righteousness for more than a decade.

sentences.zh: 至宣宗晚年，以文宗長且賢，欲付大業，猶未決。

translations.literal: By the late years of the Xuanzong reign, because Wenzong was the eldest and virtuous, the emperor wished to entrust him with the great enterprise but had not yet decided.
translations.idiomatic: In the late years of Emperor Xuanzong's reign, the emperor wished to entrust the succession to Wenzong, who was both the eldest son and regarded as virtuous, but he had not yet made up his mind.

sentences.zh: 會校獵南苑，諸皇子皆從，恭親王奕訢獲禽最多，文宗未發一矢，問之，對曰：「時方春，鳥獸孳育，不忍傷生以乾天和。

translations.literal: It happened that during a hunting drill in the Southern Park all the princes followed; Prince Gong Yixin took the most game, while Wenzong did not loose a single arrow. When asked, he replied: "It is now spring, and birds and beasts are breeding; I cannot bear to harm life and disturb Heaven's harmony."
translations.idiomatic: Once, during a hunting exercise in the Southern Park, all the princes took part. Prince Gong Yixin brought down the most game, but Wenzong did not shoot a single arrow. When asked why, he answered: "It is spring, and birds and beasts are breeding; I cannot bear to take life and disturb the harmony of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」宣宗大悅，曰：「此真帝者之言！

translations.literal: " The Emperor was greatly pleased and said: "These are truly the words of an emperor!"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was greatly pleased and exclaimed: "These are truly the words of one destined to rule!"

sentences.zh: 」立儲遂密定，受田輔導之力也。

translations.literal: " The designation of the heir was thus secretly settled, through the force of Shoutian's guidance.
translations.idiomatic: " The choice of heir was thus quietly settled—owing in large part to Shoutian's tutelage.

sentences.zh: 三十年，文宗即位，加太子太傅，兼署吏部尚書，調刑部尚書、協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year Wenzong ascended the throne; Shoutian was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, concurrently acting Minister of Personnel, then transferred to Minister of Justice and appointed Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, when Wenzong ascended the throne, Shoutian was made grand tutor of the heir apparent, served concurrently as acting minister of personnel, and was then transferred to minister of justice and appointed associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 受田雖未入樞廷，國家大政及進退大臣，上必諮而後行。

translations.literal: Although Shoutian had not entered the Grand Council, on great affairs of state and the appointment or dismissal of ministers the emperor always consulted him before acting.
translations.idiomatic: Although Shoutian never sat on the Grand Council, the emperor always consulted him before acting on major state affairs or the appointment and dismissal of high officials.

sentences.zh: 廣西軍事亟，受田數陳方略，薦林則徐、週天爵，先後起用。

translations.literal: As the military situation in Guangxi grew urgent, Shoutian repeatedly set forth strategies and recommended Lin Zexu and Zhou Tianjue, who were successively recalled to service.
translations.idiomatic: As the military crisis in Guangxi intensified, Shoutian repeatedly proposed strategies and recommended Lin Zexu and Zhou Tianjue, both of whom were eventually brought back into service.

sentences.zh: 提督向榮老於軍事，以同列不和被謗，力陳輿論，數保全之。

translations.literal: The provincial military commander Xiang Rong, experienced in warfare, was slandered because of discord among his peers; Shoutian forcefully cited public opinion and several times secured his preservation.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial military commander Xiang Rong was a seasoned soldier but came under attack because of friction with his colleagues. Shoutian repeatedly invoked public opinion on his behalf and several times saved him from dismissal.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，調管禮部。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was transferred to supervise the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xianfeng reign he was transferred to head the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二年，因河決豐北久未塞，山東、江北被災重，命偕福州將軍怡良往治賑務。

translations.literal: In the second year, because the breach of the Yellow River at Fengbei had long gone unrepaired and Shandong and the north of the Yangtze suffered severe disaster, he was ordered to go with Fuzhou General Yiliang to manage relief affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, because the Yellow River breach at Fengbei had long remained unrepaired and Shandong and the region north of the Yangtze had suffered severe flooding, he was ordered to accompany the Fuzhou general Yiliang to oversee relief work.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「災廣民眾，賑恤不可緩，尤在得人。

translations.literal: In a memorial he stated: "The disaster is widespread and the people are numerous; relief cannot be delayed, and above all the right men must be found."
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "The disaster covers a wide area and affects vast numbers of people; relief cannot be delayed, and success depends above all on appointing the right men."

sentences.zh: 」薦山東布政使劉源灝、江寧布政使祁宿藻，皆持正有為，責成專任；

translations.literal: " He recommended Shandong Provincial Administration Commissioner Liu Yuanhao and Jiangning Provincial Administration Commissioner Qi Suzao, both upright and capable, to be charged with sole responsibility;
translations.idiomatic: " He recommended Liu Yuanhao, provincial administration commissioner of Shandong, and Qi Suzao, provincial administration commissioner of Jiangning—both upright and capable men—and urged that they be given sole charge of the work;

sentences.zh: 請截留江、廣漕米六十萬石分給兩省；

translations.literal: he requested that six hundred thousand piculs of tribute grain from Jiangsu and Guangdong be retained and distributed between the two provinces;
translations.idiomatic: he asked that six hundred thousand piculs of tribute grain from the Jiangsu and Guangdong routes be held back and divided between the two provinces;

sentences.zh: 詔並允行。

translations.literal: and an edict approved all these measures.
translations.idiomatic: and an edict approved all of these proposals.

sentences.zh: 受田自侍文宗學，未嘗離左右，當陛辭，不覺感戀流涕。

translations.literal: Shoutian had attended Wenzong's studies and never left his side; when taking leave at court he could not help weeping with affection.
translations.idiomatic: Shoutian had served at Wenzong's side throughout his studies and had never been far from him. When he took formal leave at court, he wept uncontrollably with emotion.

sentences.zh: 在途觸暑染疫，力疾治事，與源灝、宿藻等覈定施賑章程，疏陳而不言病，至清江浦遽卒。

translations.literal: On the road he contracted epidemic disease in the summer heat but forced himself to attend to affairs; with Yuanhao, Suzao, and others he verified relief regulations and memorialized without mentioning his illness, and suddenly died at Qingjiangpu.
translations.idiomatic: On the journey he fell ill with an epidemic fever brought on by the summer heat, yet he pressed on with his duties. Working with Yuanhao, Suzao, and others, he finalized the relief regulations and submitted memorials without mentioning his illness, then died suddenly at Qingjiangpu.

sentences.zh: 遺疏念賊氛未靖，河患未平，尤以敬天法祖、勤政愛民、崇節儉、慎好惡、平賞罰為言。

translations.literal: His final memorial noted that the bandit threat was not yet pacified and the river calamity not yet settled, and especially urged reverence for Heaven and adherence to ancestral ways, diligent government and love for the people, esteem for frugality, caution in likes and dislikes, and fairness in rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In his final memorial he noted that the rebels had not yet been subdued and the river disaster remained unresolved, and he especially urged reverence for Heaven and fidelity to ancestral precedent, diligent governance and care for the people, frugality, circumspection in personal preferences, and even-handed rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 文宗震悼，贈太師、大學士，入祀賢良祠，賜金五千兩治喪，遣近臣慰視其父堮，擢其子檢討翰為庶子，孫三人並賜舉人。

translations.literal: Wenzong was deeply shaken; Shoutian was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and Grand Secretary, entered for worship in the Shrine of Worthies, given five thousand taels of silver for funeral expenses, and a close attendant was sent to comfort his father Fu; his son the reviser Han was promoted to junior mentor, and three grandsons were all granted the status of provincial graduates.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong was stricken with grief. Shoutian was posthumously made grand preceptor and grand secretary, enshrined in the Shrine of Worthies, and granted five thousand taels of silver for funeral expenses. A close attendant was sent to console his father Fu. His son Han, a reviser at the Hanlin Academy, was promoted to junior mentor, and all three grandsons were granted the status of provincial graduates.

sentences.zh: 复特詔曰：「杜受田品端學粹，正色立朝，皇考深加倚重，特簡為朕師傅。

translations.literal: A special edict further stated: "Du Shoutian's character was upright and his learning pure; he stood in court with proper dignity. My late father placed great trust in him and specially selected him as my tutor."
translations.idiomatic: A special edict further declared: "Du Shoutian was upright in character and pure in learning; he stood in court with unwavering integrity. My late father placed great trust in him and specially chose him as my tutor."

sentences.zh: 憶在書齋，凡所陳說，悉本唐、虞、三代聖聖相傳之旨，實能發明蘊奧，體用兼賅。

translations.literal: "Recalling our time in the study, everything he expounded was founded on the teachings handed down from the sage rulers of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties; he truly could elucidate hidden profundities and unite substance and function."
translations.idiomatic: "I recall our days in the study: everything he taught drew on the teachings handed down from the sage rulers of antiquity through the Three Dynasties; he truly could illuminate their deepest meaning and unite principle with practice."

sentences.zh: 朕即位後，週諮時政利弊，民生疾苦，盡心獻替，啟沃良多！

translations.literal: "After I ascended the throne, I constantly consulted him on the strengths and weaknesses of current policy and the hardships of the people's livelihood; he devoted his heart to counsel and greatly enriched my understanding!"
translations.idiomatic: "After my accession I constantly sought his counsel on the strengths and failings of current policy and the hardships of the people; he gave his whole heart to advising me and enriched my understanding immeasurably!"

sentences.zh: 援嘉慶朝大學士硃珪故事，特諡文正。

translations.literal: "Citing the precedent of Grand Secretary Zhu Gui in the Jiaqing reign, he was specially given the posthumous title Wenzheng."
translations.idiomatic: "Following the precedent of Grand Secretary Zhu Gui under the Jiaqing emperor, he was specially granted the posthumous title Wenzheng."

sentences.zh: 」謂其公忠正直，足當「正」字而無愧。

translations.literal: " It was said that his public loyalty and upright integrity fully deserved the character "zheng" without reproach.
translations.idiomatic: " The title was meant to signify that his public loyalty and upright integrity fully deserved the character zheng without reproach.

sentences.zh: 柩至京，上親奠，撫棺哭甚哀，晉其父堮禮部尚書銜。

translations.literal: When the coffin reached the capital the emperor personally offered libation, stroked the coffin and wept bitterly, and advanced his father Fu to the nominal rank of Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin reached the capital, the emperor personally offered libations, stroked the coffin, and wept bitterly. He also advanced Shoutian's father Fu to the nominal rank of minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 明年，上臨雍講學，复詔褒受田曩日講貫之功，即家賜祭一壇。

translations.literal: The following year, when the emperor lectured at the Imperial Academy, another edict praised Shoutian's former teaching achievements and granted a sacrificial altar at his home.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the emperor lectured at the Imperial Academy, another edict praised Shoutian's years of instruction and granted a sacrificial altar to be offered at his home.

sentences.zh: 及柩歸，命恭親王奠送，遣官到籍致祭，飾終之典，一時無與比。

translations.literal: When the coffin returned home, Prince Gong was ordered to offer libation on the journey; officials were dispatched to his native place to perform sacrifices; the funeral honors were unmatched in that age.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin was returned to his native place, Prince Gong was ordered to escort it and offer libations along the way; officials were sent to his home district to perform sacrifices. The funeral honors accorded him were unequaled in his time.

sentences.zh: 子，由翰林院編修累官戶部侍郎，督辦山東團練。

translations.literal: His son, rising from Hanlin Academy compiler to Vice Minister of Revenue, supervised Shandong militia training.
translations.idiomatic: His son advanced from compiler at the Hanlin Academy to vice minister of revenue and supervised militia training in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 翰，字繼園。

translations.literal: Han, styled Jiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Han, whose courtesy name was Jiyuan.

sentences.zh: 道光二十四年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the twenty-fourth year of Daoguang, he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the twenty-fourth year of the Daoguang reign, was chosen as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed a reviser.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，降。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng he was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Xianfeng reign he was demoted.

sentences.zh: 服闋，補庶子。

translations.literal: After mourning ended he was restored as junior mentor.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning period ended, he was restored to the post of junior mentor.

sentences.zh: 文宗念受田舊勞，數月間迭擢工部侍郎，命在軍機大臣上行走，辦理京城巡防事宜。

translations.literal: Wenzong, mindful of Shoutian's old service, within a few months successively promoted him to Vice Minister of Works and ordered him to serve above the Grand Council ministers in managing capital patrol and defense affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Shoutian's long service, Wenzong promoted Han within a few months to vice minister of works and ordered him to serve above the Grand Council ministers in charge of capital patrol and defense.

sentences.zh: 翰勇於任事，甚被倚任。

translations.literal: Han was bold in undertaking affairs and greatly relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Han was bold in taking on responsibility and came to be greatly relied upon.

sentences.zh: 十年，隨扈熱河，以勞賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he accompanied the entourage to Rehe and was granted the peacock feather for his labors.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he accompanied the court to Rehe and was awarded the peacock feather for his exertions.

sentences.zh: 上崩於行在，穆宗即位。

translations.literal: The emperor died at the traveling palace and Muzong ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor died at the traveling palace, and the future Emperor Muzong ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 御史董元醇疏請兩宮皇太后垂簾聽政，載垣、端華、肅順等持不可，翰附之，抗言甚力，遂黜元醇議。

translations.literal: Censor Dong Yuanchun memorialized requesting that the two empress dowagers rule from behind the curtain; Zaiyuan, Duhua, Sushun, and others held this impossible; Han sided with them and argued forcefully, and Dong's proposal was rejected.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Dong Yuanchun memorialized asking that the two empress dowagers rule from behind a curtain. Zaiyuan, Duhua, Sushun, and others opposed the idea; Han sided with them and argued vigorously, and Dong's proposal was set aside.

sentences.zh: 肅順曰：「君誠不愧杜文正之子也！

translations.literal: Sushun said: "You truly do not dishonor the son of Du Wenzheng!"
translations.idiomatic: Sushun said: "You are indeed a worthy son of Du Wenzheng!"

sentences.zh: 」既而載垣等以竊奪政柄被罪，翰連坐，議革職戍新疆，詔原之，褫職，免其發遣。

translations.literal: " Soon after, Zaiyuan and others were punished for usurping power; Han was implicated, and it was proposed to strip his office and exile him to Xinjiang; an edict pardoned him, removed his post, and exempted him from deportation.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long Zaiyuan and the others were condemned for seizing power. Han was implicated as well; it was proposed to strip him of office and exile him to Xinjiang, but an edict pardoned him, removed him from office, and spared him deportation.

sentences.zh: 同治五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tongzhi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of the Tongzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 祁俊藻，字春圃，山西壽陽人。

translations.literal: Qi Junzao, styled Chunpu, was a native of Shouyang, Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Junzao, whose courtesy name was Chunpu, came from Shouyang in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 父韻士，官戶部郎中，以事繫獄。

translations.literal: His father Yunshi served as a director in the Ministry of Revenue and was imprisoned on account of an affair.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yunshi held the post of director in the Ministry of Revenue and was imprisoned in connection with an official matter.

sentences.zh: 俊藻方幼，隨侍讀書不輟，賦春草詩以見志。

translations.literal: Junzao was still young; he attended his father without ceasing his studies and composed a poem on spring grass to express his resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Junzao was still a boy. He attended his father in prison without interrupting his studies and wrote a poem on spring grass to express his determination.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十九年，成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Jiaqing he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of the Jiaqing reign he passed the metropolitan examination, was chosen as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，直南書房。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he served in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Daoguang reign he was assigned to the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 督湖南學政，累遷庶子。

translations.literal: He supervised educational administration in Hunan and was successively promoted to junior mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as educational commissioner of Hunan and was promoted in stages to junior mentor.

sentences.zh: 十年，以母病陳情歸養，宣宗不許，予假省親。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, citing his mother's illness he petitioned to return home to care for her; the Xuanzong Emperor did not permit it but granted leave to visit his parents.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, citing his mother's illness, he petitioned to return home to care for her. Emperor Xuanzong refused permission but granted him leave to visit his family.

sentences.zh: 逾年回京，補原官，遷侍講學士。

translations.literal: After more than a year he returned to the capital, resumed his former post, and was promoted to expositor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he returned to the capital, resumed his former post, and was promoted to expositor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 尋复予假省母，不開缺。

translations.literal: Soon he was again granted leave to visit his mother, without vacating his post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was again granted leave to visit his mother, without vacating his post.

sentences.zh: 歷通政司副使、光祿寺卿、內閣學士。

translations.literal: He successively served as Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission, Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission, director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and grand secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸，十六年，將屆服闋，預授兵部侍郎，督江蘇學政。

translations.literal: He returned home for his mother's mourning; in the sixteenth year, as his mourning period was about to end, he was pre-appointed Vice Minister of War and supervisor of educational administration in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to observe mourning for his mother. In the sixteenth year, as his mourning period was nearing its end, he was appointed in advance as vice minister of war and educational commissioner of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 歷戶部、吏部侍郎，留學政任，未滿，十九年，命偕侍郎黃爵滋視福建海防及禁煙事，連擢左都御史、兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He served successively as Vice Minister of Revenue and Vice Minister of Personnel, retaining his educational commission before its term expired; in the nineteenth year he was ordered with Vice Minister Huang Juezi to inspect Fujian coastal defense and opium prohibition, and was successively promoted to Censor-in-Chief of the Left and Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as vice minister of revenue and vice minister of personnel while retaining his educational commission before its term had expired. In the nineteenth year he was ordered, together with Vice Minister Huang Juezi, to inspect Fujian coastal defense and the opium prohibition effort, and was promoted in quick succession to censor-in-chief of the left and minister of war.

sentences.zh: 迭疏陳總宜駐泉州治防務，改海口砲台為墩，查禁煙販，捕治漢奸，並禁漳、泉兩府行使夷錢，夾帶私鑄者治罪，嚴懲械鬥，並得旨允行。

translations.literal: In successive memorials he stated that the commander-in-chief should station himself at Quanzhou to manage defense, that coastal batteries should be converted to blockhouses, that opium trafficking should be investigated and banned, Han traitors captured and punished, and that Zhangzhou and Quanzhou prefectures should be forbidden to circulate foreign coin, with those mixing in private casting punished, and armed brawls severely punished; all received imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: In a series of memorials he urged that the commander-in-chief station himself at Quanzhou to direct coastal defense, that harbor batteries be converted into blockhouses, that opium trafficking be investigated and suppressed, and that Han collaborators be arrested and punished. He also called for a ban on foreign coin in Zhangzhou and Quanzhou prefectures, with penalties for those mixing in privately cast currency, and for severe punishment of armed brawls. All of these proposals received imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 在閩半載，還經浙江，按台、溫兩府私種罌粟，劾罷台州知府潘盛；

translations.literal: After half a year in Fujian, returning by way of Zhejiang he investigated private opium cultivation in Taizhou and Wenzhou prefectures and impeached Taizhou Prefect Pan Sheng, who was dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: After half a year in Fujian, he returned by way of Zhejiang and investigated private opium cultivation in Taizhou and Wenzhou prefectures, impeaching Taizhou prefect Pan Sheng, who was dismissed;

sentences.zh: 又劾溫州知府劉煜試行票鹽不善，被議，自呈枉屈，戍新疆。

translations.literal: he also impeached Wenzhou Prefect Liu Yu for mismanaging the trial of ticket salt, was himself censured, presented a memorial claiming wrongful punishment, and was exiled to Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: he also impeached Wenzhou prefect Liu Yu for mismanaging a trial of the ticket-salt system. Junzao himself was censured, submitted a memorial claiming he had been wronged, and was exiled to Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 時鄧廷楨奏擊英吉利兵船於廈門走之，忌者謂其不實，命俊藻復往按，具陳戰胜狀。

translations.literal: At that time Deng Tingzhen memorialized that he had routed English warships at Xiamen; jealous parties said this was untrue, and Junzao was ordered to reinvestigate and fully reported the circumstances of victory.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Deng Tingzhen reported that he had driven off British warships at Xiamen. Envious officials claimed the report was false, and Junzao was ordered back to investigate. He submitted a full account confirming the victory.

sentences.zh: 回京，仍直南書房。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he again served in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to the capital he was again assigned to the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，調戶部，命為軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue and appointed a Grand Council minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue and appointed a Grand Council minister.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，偕尚書文慶按長蘆鹽運使陳鑑挪撥鹽課，彌補加價，褫其職，歷任鹽政運司議譴有差。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, together with Minister Wen Qing he investigated Changlu Salt Transport Commissioner Chen Jian for diverting salt revenue to cover price supplements; Chen was stripped of office and successive salt administrators and transport commissioners were censured to varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, together with Minister Wen Qing, he investigated Changlu salt transport commissioner Chen Jian for diverting salt revenue to cover price supplements. Chen was stripped of office, and successive salt administrators and transport commissioners were censured to varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，以戶部尚書協辦大學士，命赴甘肅偕琦善按前任總督布彥泰清查舛誤、縱容家丁，下嚴議。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, as Minister of Revenue and Associate Grand Secretary, he was ordered to Gansu with Qishan to investigate former Governor Buyantai for errors in audit and indulgence of household retainers; severe censure was imposed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, as minister of revenue and associate grand secretary, he was ordered to Gansu with Qishan to investigate former governor Buyantai for errors in auditing accounts and indulgence of household retainers. Severe censure was imposed.

sentences.zh: 回京，請便道省墓，途次聞宣宗崩，過里門不入。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital he requested to visit his ancestral graves by a convenient route; on the way he heard that Xuanzong had died and passed his home gate without entering.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to the capital he asked permission to visit his ancestral graves by a convenient route. Along the way he learned that Emperor Xuanzong had died and passed his home without entering.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，拜體仁閣大學士，仍管戶部。

translations.literal: When Wenzong ascended the throne, Junzao was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Embodying Benevolence and continued to supervise the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong ascended the throne, Junzao was made grand secretary of the Hall of Embodying Benevolence while continuing to head the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 俊藻自道光中論洋務與穆彰阿不合，至是文宗銳意圖治，罷穆彰阿，俊藻遂領樞務，開言路，起用舊臣，俊藻左右之。

translations.literal: Junzao had disagreed with Mu Zhang'a on foreign affairs since the Daoguang reign; now Wenzong was keen to govern well, dismissed Mu Zhang'a, and Junzao then led Grand Council affairs, opened the channels of remonstrance, and recalled old officials—Junzao guiding these measures.
translations.idiomatic: Junzao had been at odds with Mu Zhang'a over foreign affairs since the Daoguang reign. Now Wenzong was determined to set the government in order, dismissed Mu Zhang'a, and Junzao took charge of Grand Council affairs, reopened channels for memorialists, and brought back veteran officials—initiatives that Junzao helped steer.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，調管工部，兼管戶部三庫事務。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was transferred to supervise the Ministry of Works and concurrently the three treasuries of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xianfeng reign he was transferred to head the Ministry of Works and was also put in charge of the three treasuries of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二年，復調戶部。

translations.literal: In the second year he was again transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was transferred back to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 廣西匪日熾，出湖南，遂不可製，湖北、江南數省先後淪陷。

translations.literal: The bandits in Guangxi grew fiercer daily, spilled into Hunan, and could no longer be controlled; several provinces including Hubei and Jiangnan successively fell.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels in Guangxi grew stronger by the day, spilled into Hunan, and could no longer be contained. Hubei, Jiangnan, and several other provinces fell in succession.

sentences.zh: 軍興財匱，議者試行鈔法，又鑄當百、當五百大錢，皆行之未久而滋弊。

translations.literal: With war arising finances were exhausted; advocates tried paper currency and also cast large coins worth one hundred and five hundred cash; all were implemented briefly before abuses multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: War had drained the treasury, and advocates experimented with paper currency and also cast large coins denominated at one hundred and five hundred cash. All were tried briefly before serious abuses appeared.

sentences.zh: 尚書肅順同掌戶部事，尚苛刻。

translations.literal: Minister Sushun jointly managed Revenue affairs and was still harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Sushun shared responsibility for revenue affairs and remained harsh in his methods.

sentences.zh: 又湘軍初起，肅順力言其可用，上鄉之，俊藻皆意與齟《齒吾》，屢稱病請罷，溫詔慰留。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the Xiang Army was first raised, Sushun strongly argued it could be used and the emperor inclined toward this view; Junzao's views clashed on every point, he repeatedly pleaded illness to resign, and warm edicts urged him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xiang Army was first organized, Sushun strongly argued for its usefulness and won the emperor's favor. Junzao disagreed on nearly every point, repeatedly pleaded illness to resign, and received warm edicts urging him to stay.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，复堅以為請，乃允致仕。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year he again firmly requested retirement, and permission to leave office was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourth year he again pressed his request firmly, and permission to retire was granted.

sentences.zh: 十年，英法聯軍犯天津，車駕將幸熱河，俊藻密疏切諫。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Anglo-French allied armies threatened Tianjin; the imperial carriage was about to proceed to Rehe, and Junzao submitted a secret memorial urgently remonstrating.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the Anglo-French allied armies threatened Tianjin. As the court prepared to move to Rehe, Junzao submitted a secret memorial urgently remonstrating against the move.

sentences.zh: 又言關中形勝可建都，釐捐病民，北省尤宜急停，並報聞。

translations.literal: He also stated that the strategic advantages of Guanzhong made it suitable for establishing the capital, that the lijin levy harmed the people and should especially be halted quickly in the northern provinces, and reported these views.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that the strategic advantages of the Guanzhong region made it suitable as a capital site, that the lijin transit levy harmed the people and should be halted quickly in the northern provinces in particular, and reported these views to the throne.

sentences.zh: 十一年，穆宗即位，特詔起用。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Muzong ascended the throne and a special edict recalled him to service.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, when Muzong ascended the throne, a special edict recalled him to office.

sentences.zh: 疏陳時政六事：曰保護聖躬以崇帝學；

translations.literal: In a memorial he set forth six matters of current policy: first, protect the sacred person to honor imperial learning;
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he set forth six urgent matters of policy: first, protect the emperor's person in order to honor imperial learning;

sentences.zh: 曰綏輯民心以清盜源；

translations.literal: second, pacify popular sentiment to clear the source of banditry;
translations.idiomatic: second, pacify the people's hearts in order to cut off the roots of rebellion;

sentences.zh: 曰重守令以固民心；

translations.literal: third, value prefects and magistrates to solidify popular hearts;
translations.idiomatic: third, place greater weight on prefects and magistrates in order to secure the people's loyalty;

sentences.zh: 曰開制科以收人才；

translations.literal: fourth, open special examinations to gather talent;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, open special examinations to recruit talent;

sentences.zh: 曰速剿山東、河南賊匪，嚴防山西、陝西要隘，以衛畿輔；

translations.literal: fifth, swiftly suppress bandits in Shandong and Henan and strictly guard key passes in Shanxi and Shaanxi to protect the capital region;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, swiftly suppress the rebels in Shandong and Henan and strictly guard the key passes of Shanxi and Shaanxi in order to protect the capital region;

sentences.zh: 曰敦崇節儉以培元氣。

translations.literal: sixth, earnestly promote frugality to nourish vital energy.
translations.idiomatic: sixth, earnestly promote frugality in order to restore the nation's vitality.

sentences.zh: 言甚切摯，並被嘉納，次第施行。

translations.literal: His words were very earnest and sincere, and all were praised and accepted, being implemented in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: His language was earnest and sincere. All six proposals were praised and accepted, and were carried out in turn.

sentences.zh: 命以大學士銜授禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was ordered to be appointed Minister of Rites with the nominal rank of Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed minister of rites with the nominal rank of grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，穆宗入學，命直弘德殿，偕翁心存、倭仁、李鴻藻同授讀，摘錄經史二帙進呈。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, when Muzong entered his studies, he was ordered to serve in the Hall of Manifest Virtue, together with Weng Xincun, Woren, and Li Hongzao to instruct jointly, and compiled two volumes of selections from the classics and histories for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tongzhi reign, when Muzong began his studies, Junzao was assigned to the Hall of Manifest Virtue to teach jointly with Weng Xincun, Woren, and Li Hongzao, and compiled two volumes of selections from the classics and histories for presentation to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上讀大學畢，俊藻具疏推陳為人君止於仁之義，略曰：「大學一書，皇上已成誦，凡制治保邦之道，用人行政之源，胥在於是。

translations.literal: When the emperor finished reading the Great Learning, Junzao submitted a detailed memorial expounding the meaning that for the ruler of men the ultimate goal is benevolence, stating in summary: "Your Majesty has already completed recitation of the Great Learning; all principles of ordering government and preserving the state, and the sources of employing men and administering affairs, lie therein."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor had finished reading the Great Learning, Junzao submitted a detailed memorial expounding the doctrine that the ruler's ultimate goal is benevolence. In summary he wrote: "Your Majesty has already completed recitation of the Great Learning. Every principle of ordering government and preserving the state, and every source of employing men and administering affairs, lies within it."

sentences.zh: 為人君之道，止於仁而已。

translations.literal: The way of the ruler of men ends in benevolence alone.
translations.idiomatic: The way of the ruler ends in benevolence and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 治國平天下兩章，言仁者六，終之以未有上好仁而下不好義。

translations.literal: The two chapters on bringing order to the state and pacifying the realm speak of benevolence six times and conclude with the statement that never has there been one above who loved benevolence while those below did not love righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The two chapters on bringing order to the state and pacifying the realm mention benevolence six times and conclude with the statement that never has a ruler above loved benevolence while those below did not love righteousness.

sentences.zh: 蓋仁者必以仁親為寶，故能愛人，能惡人。

translations.literal: For the benevolent must take benevolent kinship as treasure, and thus can love men and can hate men.
translations.idiomatic: For the benevolent ruler must take benevolent kinship as his treasure, and thus can love the worthy and hate the unworthy.

sentences.zh: 不好仁，則好人之所惡，惡人之所好。

translations.literal: If one does not love benevolence, one loves what good men hate and hates what good men love.
translations.idiomatic: If one does not love benevolence, one loves what good men hate and hates what good men love.

sentences.zh: 仁者必以貪為戒，故忠信以得之，不仁者則驕泰以失之矣。

translations.literal: The benevolent must take greed as a warning, and thus gain it through loyalty and trust; the non-benevolent lose it through arrogance and excess.
translations.idiomatic: The benevolent ruler must take greed as a warning, and thus gains the realm through loyalty and trust; the non-benevolent lose it through arrogance and excess.

sentences.zh: 仁者以義為利，不以利為利，故以財發身，不仁者則以身發財，菑害並至矣。

translations.literal: The benevolent take righteousness as profit, not profit as profit; thus they use wealth to extend the person. The non-benevolent use the person to extend wealth, and calamity and harm arrive together.
translations.idiomatic: The benevolent take righteousness as profit, not profit as profit; thus they use wealth to enrich life. The non-benevolent use life to amass wealth, and calamity and harm arrive together.

sentences.zh: 千古治亂之機，判於義利，而義利之判，則由於上之好仁不好仁也。

translations.literal: The pivot of order and disorder through the ages is decided between righteousness and profit, and the decision between righteousness and profit depends on whether those above love benevolence or do not.
translations.idiomatic: The pivot of order and disorder through the ages turns on the choice between righteousness and profit, and that choice depends on whether those above love benevolence or do not.

sentences.zh: 如近日所講帝鑑圖說，下車泣罪，解網施恩，澤及枯骨等事，斯即帝王仁心所見端也。

translations.literal: As in the recent lectures on the Illustrated Mirror of Emperors—descending from the carriage to weep over crimes, releasing the net to show mercy, extending grace even to withered bones—these are the first signs of the benevolent heart of an emperor.
translations.idiomatic: As in the recent lectures on the Illustrated Mirror of Emperors—descending from the carriage to weep over a prisoner's crime, releasing animals from the net to show mercy, extending grace even to withered bones—these are the first signs of an emperor's benevolent heart.

sentences.zh: 若納諫求賢，尊儒遠佞，則仁親為寶，能好能惡之說也。

translations.literal: As for accepting remonstrance and seeking the worthy, honoring Confucian learning and keeping distant from flatterers—these are the teachings on taking benevolent kinship as treasure and being able to love and hate.
translations.idiomatic: As for accepting remonstrance, seeking the worthy, honoring Confucian learning, and keeping flatterers at a distance—these embody the teaching on taking benevolent kinship as treasure and being able to love the worthy and hate the unworthy.

sentences.zh: 露台罷工，裘馬卻獻，則以義為利，不以利為利之說也。

translations.literal: Halting work on the terrace stage and declining gifts of fur and horses—these illustrate the teaching of taking righteousness as profit, not profit as profit.
translations.idiomatic: Halting work on the terrace stage and declining gifts of fur and horses—these embody the teaching of taking righteousness as profit rather than profit as profit.

sentences.zh: 帝鑑圖說講畢，請進講輿地，以會典諸圖簡明，易於指畫。

translations.literal: When lectures on the Illustrated Mirror of Emperors were completed, he requested to proceed to geography, since the maps in the Collected Statutes were concise and easy to illustrate.
translations.idiomatic: When the lectures on the Illustrated Mirror of Emperors were finished, he asked to proceed to geography, noting that the maps in the Collected Statutes were concise and easy to use for instruction.

sentences.zh: 又耕織圖及內府石刻宋馬遠豳風圖為農桑衣食之原，皇上讀書之暇，隨時講求，庶知稼穡之艱難，懍守成之不易也。

translations.literal: He also cited the Pictures of Tilling and Weaving and the inner palace stone engravings of Song Ma Yuan's Bin Feng illustrations as the source of farming, sericulture, clothing, and food, urging that in His Majesty's leisure from reading he study these at all times, so as to know the hardship of cultivation and revere the difficulty of preserving what has been achieved.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended the Pictures of Tilling and Weaving and the palace stone engravings of Song Ma Yuan's Bin Feng illustrations as the foundations of agriculture, sericulture, clothing, and food. He urged that in His Majesty's leisure from reading he study these regularly, so as to understand the hardship of farming and appreciate how difficult it is to preserve what has been achieved.

sentences.zh: 二年，上服除，俊藻偕倭仁、李鴻藻上疏曰：「皇上沖齡踐阼，智慧漸開。

translations.literal: In the second year, when the emperor's mourning ended, Junzao together with Woren and Li Hongzao submitted a memorial stating: "Your Majesty ascended the throne at a tender age, and your wisdom is gradually unfolding."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when the emperor's mourning period ended, Junzao joined Woren and Li Hongzao in a memorial that read: "Your Majesty ascended the throne at a tender age, and your wisdom is gradually unfolding."

sentences.zh: 當此釋服之初，吉禮舉行，聖心之敬肆於此分，風會之轉移即於此始，則玩好之漸可慮也，遊觀之漸可慮也，興作之漸可慮也。

translations.literal: At this beginning when mourning garments are laid aside and auspicious rites are performed, the reverence or laxity of the sacred heart is decided at this juncture, and the turning of custom begins here—then the gradual growth of fondness for curios is to be feared, the gradual growth of sightseeing is to be feared, and the gradual growth of construction projects is to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: At this moment when mourning garments are laid aside and auspicious rites are performed, whether the imperial mind will remain reverent or grow lax is decided now, and the turning of custom begins here. The gradual growth of fondness for curios is to be feared, as is the gradual growth of sightseeing and of grand construction projects.

sentences.zh: 嗜好之端一開，不惟分誦讀之心，海內之窺意旨者，且將從風而靡。

translations.literal: Once the first opening of indulgence appears, it will not only divide the heart devoted to study; those throughout the realm who watch for imperial intent will also follow the wind and fall into excess.
translations.idiomatic: Once the first indulgence appears, it will not only distract the mind from study; those throughout the realm who watch for imperial intent will follow suit and fall into excess.

sentences.zh: 安危治亂之機，其端甚微，所關甚鉅，可無慎乎？

translations.literal: The pivot of safety and danger, order and disorder, begins in something very slight yet concerns matters very great—can one not be cautious?
translations.idiomatic: The pivot of safety and danger, order and disorder, begins in something very slight yet concerns matters of the greatest moment—can one not be cautious?

sentences.zh: 方今軍務未平，生民塗炭，正君臣交儆之時，非上下恬熙之日。

translations.literal: At present military affairs are not yet settled and the people are in misery; this is precisely the time when ruler and ministers should warn one another, not a day for ease and complacency above and below.
translations.idiomatic: At present military affairs are not yet settled and the people are in misery. This is precisely the time when ruler and ministers should warn one another, not a day for ease and complacency throughout the court.

sentences.zh: 伏原皇上恪遵慈訓，時時以憂勤惕厲為心，以逸樂便安為戒。

translations.literal: We humbly pray that Your Majesty faithfully follow the gracious instruction, always taking anxious diligence and vigilance as your heart, and taking ease, pleasure, and comfortable security as your warning.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly pray that Your Majesty faithfully follow the empress dowagers' instruction, always taking anxious diligence and vigilance to heart, and regarding ease, pleasure, and comfortable security as warnings.

sentences.zh: 凡內廷服禦一切用項，稍涉浮靡，概從裁減；

translations.literal: As for all items of clothing and use within the inner palace, whatever is slightly extravagant should in general be cut back;
translations.idiomatic: As for all items of clothing and daily use within the inner palace, whatever is even slightly extravagant should be cut back;

sentences.zh: 向例所有，不妨量為撙節。

translations.literal: what has been customary may suitably be restrained in measure.
translations.idiomatic: and what has long been customary may suitably be restrained in measure.

sentences.zh: 如是，則外務之紛華不接於耳目，詩書之啟迪益斂夫心思，聖學日新，聖德日固，而去奢崇儉之風，自不令而行矣。

translations.literal: If so, then the splendor of external affairs will not reach the eyes and ears, the enlightenment of poetry and books will increasingly gather the mind, sacred learning will daily renew, sacred virtue will daily strengthen, and the wind of rejecting extravagance and honoring frugality will of itself prevail without being commanded.
translations.idiomatic: If so, the splendor of external affairs will not reach the eyes and ears, the enlightenment of the classics will increasingly focus the mind, imperial learning will daily advance, imperial virtue will daily strengthen, and the spirit of rejecting extravagance and honoring frugality will prevail of itself without needing to be commanded.

sentences.zh: 」疏上，優詔褒答焉。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, a gracious edict praised and answered it.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, an edict warmly praised and answered it.

sentences.zh: 俊藻提倡樸學，延納寒素，士林歸之。

translations.literal: Junzao promoted plain learning, received poor scholars of humble origin, and the scholarly world rallied to him.
translations.idiomatic: Junzao promoted plain scholarship, welcomed scholars of humble means, and the scholarly world rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「通經之學，義理與訓詁不可偏重。

translations.literal: In a memorial he stated: "In the study of mastering the classics, moral principle and textual exegesis cannot be overweighted on either side."
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "In the study of the classics, moral principle and textual exegesis cannot be overweighted on either side."

sentences.zh: 後學不察，以訓詁專屬漢儒，義理專屬宋儒，使畫分界限，學術日歧。

translations.literal: Later students fail to perceive this, assigning exegesis solely to Han scholars and moral principle solely to Song scholars, drawing dividing lines so that learning daily diverges.
translations.idiomatic: Later students fail to see this, assigning exegesis solely to Han scholars and moral principle solely to Song scholars, drawing dividing lines until scholarship grows daily more fragmented.

sentences.zh: 」因舉素所知寒士端木埰、鄭珍、莫友芝、閻汝弼、王軒、楊寶臣，經明行修，堪資器使。

translations.literal: " He then cited poor scholars he had long known—Duanmu Cai, Zheng Zhen, Mo Youzhi, Yan Rubi, Wang Xuan, and Yang Baochen—clear in the classics and upright in conduct, fit to be employed.
translations.idiomatic: " He then cited poor scholars he had long known—Duanmu Cai, Zheng Zhen, Mo Youzhi, Yan Rubi, Wang Xuan, and Yang Baochen—men learned in the classics and upright in conduct, fit for appointment.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「軍興以來，不講吏治，請下中外大臣，保舉循吏及伏處潛修之士，以備任用。

translations.literal: In another memorial he stated: "Since the rise of military campaigns, local governance has been neglected. I request that ministers at court and in the provinces be ordered to recommend honest officials and scholars in hidden retirement who have cultivated themselves, to be held in readiness for appointment."
translations.idiomatic: In another memorial he wrote: "Since the wars began, local governance has been neglected. I ask that ministers at court and in the provinces be ordered to recommend honest officials and scholars in quiet retirement who have cultivated themselves, to be held in readiness for appointment."

sentences.zh: 」自舉原任同知劉大紳、按察使李文耕、大順廣道劉煦，請宣付史館入循吏傳。

translations.literal: " He himself cited former sub-prefect Liu Dashen, provincial surveillance commissioner Li Wengeng, and Da-Shun-Guang circuit intendant Liu Xu, requesting that edicts be issued ordering the Historiographical Institute to enter them in the Biographies of Honest Officials.
translations.idiomatic: " He himself cited former sub-prefect Liu Dashen, provincial surveillance commissioner Li Wengeng, and Da-Shun-Guang circuit intendant Liu Xu, asking that edicts be issued ordering the Historiographical Institute to enter them in the Biographies of Honest Officials.

sentences.zh: 又薦直隸知縣張光藻、陳崇砥、王蘭廣，山東知縣蔣慶第，山西知縣程豫、吳輝祖及江南優貢端木埰，山西舉人秦東來。

translations.literal: He also recommended Zhili magistrates Zhang Guangzao, Chen Chongdi, and Wang Languang; Shandong magistrate Jiang Qingdi; Shanxi magistrates Cheng Yu and Wu Huizu; the distinguished tribute student from Jiangnan Duanmu Cai; and the provincial graduate from Shanxi Qin Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended Zhili magistrates Zhang Guangzao, Chen Chongdi, and Wang Languang; Shandong magistrate Jiang Qingdi; Shanxi magistrates Cheng Yu and Wu Huizu; the distinguished tribute student from Jiangnan Duanmu Cai; and the provincial graduate from Shanxi Qin Donglai.

sentences.zh: 並嘉納允行。

translations.literal: All were praised and accepted for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All were praised and approved for implementation.

sentences.zh: 屢以病乞休，三年，詔致仕，食全俸。

translations.literal: He repeatedly pleaded illness to retire; in the third year an edict granted retirement with full salary.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly pleaded illness to retire. In the third year an edict granted him retirement on full salary.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒，晉贈太保，祀賢良祠，命鍾郡王奠醊，諡文端。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died and was posthumously advanced to Grand Guardian, entered for worship in the Shrine of Worthies, with Prince Zhong ordered to offer libations; he was given the posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died. He was posthumously made grand guardian, enshrined in the Shrine of Worthies, and Prince Zhong was ordered to offer libations. He was given the posthumous title Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 擢其子編修世長以侍讀用。

translations.literal: His son the compiler Shizhang was promoted for appointment as palace reader.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shizhang, a compiler at the Hanlin Academy, was promoted for appointment as palace reader.

sentences.zh: 世長，字子禾。

translations.literal: Shizhang, styled Zihe.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhang, whose courtesy name was Zihe.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the tenth year of Xianfeng.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the tenth year of the Xianfeng reign.

sentences.zh: 年十三，侍父江蘇學政任，幕客俞正燮、張穆、苗夔諸人，並樸學通儒，世長濡染有素，尤篤守宋儒義理之說。

translations.literal: At the age of thirteen he attended his father during his term as Jiangsu educational commissioner; staff members Yu Zhengxie, Zhang Mu, Miao Kui, and others were all plain-learning scholars thoroughly versed in the classics, and Shizhang was steeped in this from youth, especially devoted to the moral teachings of Song Neo-Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of thirteen he accompanied his father during his term as educational commissioner of Jiangsu. Staff members Yu Zhengxie, Zhang Mu, Miao Kui, and others were all distinguished scholars of plain learning, and Shizhang was steeped in their influence from youth, especially devoted to the moral teachings of Song Neo-Confucians.

sentences.zh: 同治九年，服闋，補侍讀。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tongzhi, when mourning ended, he was restored as palace reader.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Tongzhi reign, when his mourning period ended, he was restored to the post of palace reader.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in stages to grand secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，連督安徽、順天、浙江學政，清勤愛士，一守俊藻舊規。

translations.literal: In the early Guangxu reign he successively supervised educational administration in Anhui, Shuntian, and Zhejiang, being diligent, frugal, and fond of scholars, adhering entirely to Junzao's old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Guangxu reign he served in succession as educational commissioner of Anhui, Shuntian, and Zhejiang. Diligent, frugal, and devoted to scholars, he adhered entirely to Junzao's old standards.

sentences.zh: 歷禮部、吏部侍郎，擢​​左都御史。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Minister of Rites and Vice Minister of Personnel and was promoted to Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice minister of rites and vice minister of personnel and was promoted to censor-in-chief of the left.

sentences.zh: 十年，命偕尚書延煦勘山東河工，疏言：「非疏海口不能洩盛漲。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was ordered with Minister Yanchi to inspect Shandong river works and stated in a memorial: "Without dredging the sea mouth the great flood cannot be discharged."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was ordered, together with Minister Yanchi, to inspect Shandong river works. In a memorial he wrote: "Without dredging the sea mouth the great flood cannot be discharged."

sentences.zh: 修防以民埝為第一層屏障，守民埝即以守大堤。

translations.literal: In repair and defense the people's dikes should be the first layer of barrier; guarding the people's dikes is guarding the main embankment.
translations.idiomatic: In repair and defense the people's dikes should serve as the first line of defense; guarding the people's dikes is guarding the main embankment.

sentences.zh: 巡撫陳士傑築修民埝多在大堤既決之後，殊為失計。

translations.literal: Governor Chen Shijie built and repaired people's dikes mostly only after the main embankment had already breached—a serious error in planning.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Chen Shijie built and repaired people's dikes mostly only after the main embankment had already breached—a serious error in planning.

sentences.zh: 請乘時興修。

translations.literal: I request that repairs be undertaken while the time is right.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that repairs be undertaken while conditions permitted.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " His request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " His request was approved.

sentences.zh: 迭疏陳時務，多持正議。

translations.literal: In successive memorials on current affairs he mostly upheld upright views.
translations.idiomatic: In successive memorials on current affairs he mostly upheld upright views.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遷工部尚書，兼管順天府尹。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to Minister of Works and concurrently supervised the Shuntian prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to minister of works and was also put in charge of the Shuntian prefect.

sentences.zh: 兩典會試，皆得士。

translations.literal: He presided twice over the metropolitan examination and both times obtained worthy candidates.
translations.idiomatic: He presided twice over the metropolitan examination and both times selected worthy candidates.

sentences.zh: 世長清操自勵，累世官卿貳，家如寒素，時以稱焉。

translations.literal: Shizhang disciplined himself with pure integrity; though his family for generations held ministerial rank, their household was like that of the poor, and he was praised for this in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhang disciplined himself with pure integrity. Though his family for generations had held ministerial rank, their household lived like that of the poor, and he was praised for this in his time.

sentences.zh: 十八年，卒，優詔賜卹，諡文恪。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he died; a gracious edict granted funeral compensation and the posthumous title Wenkai.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he died. A gracious edict granted funeral compensation and the posthumous title Wenkai.

sentences.zh: 賜其孫師曾員外郎，子友蒙主事。

translations.literal: His grandson Shizeng was granted the rank of secretary in the outer court; his son Youmeng was granted the rank of director.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Shizeng was granted the rank of secretary in the outer court, and his son Youmeng was granted the rank of director.

sentences.zh: 翁心存，字二銘，江蘇常熟人。

translations.literal: Weng Xincun, styled Erming, was a native of Changshu, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Xincun, whose courtesy name was Erming, came from Changshu in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 父咸封，官海州學正。

translations.literal: His father Xianfeng served as director of studies in Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xianfeng served as director of studies in Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 知州唐仲冕見心存有異才，奇之，授之學。

translations.literal: Prefect Tang Zhongmian saw that Xincun had unusual talent, marveled at him, and taught him.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Tang Zhongmian saw that Xincun had unusual talent, took a keen interest in him, and personally instructed him.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Daoguang reign he passed the metropolitan examination, was chosen as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 大考擢中允，督廣東學政。

translations.literal: In the major examination he was promoted to middle attendant and supervised educational administration in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the triennial palace examination he was promoted to middle attendant and was appointed educational commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 任滿，入直上書房，授惠郡王讀。

translations.literal: When his term ended he entered the Upper Study and instructed Prince Hui.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was assigned to the Upper Study to instruct Prince Hui.

sentences.zh: 尋督江西學政，累遷大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: Soon he supervised educational administration in Jiangxi and was successively promoted to Vice President of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed educational commissioner of Jiangxi and was promoted in stages to vice president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 十七年，复直上書房，授六阿哥讀。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he again entered the Upper Study and instructed the Sixth Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was again assigned to the Upper Study to instruct the Sixth Prince.

sentences.zh: 逾年，以母老乞養。

translations.literal: After more than a year he petitioned to retire and care for his aged mother.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he petitioned to retire and care for his aged mother.

sentences.zh: 家居十年，終母喪。

translations.literal: He remained at home for ten years until his mother's mourning was completed.
translations.idiomatic: He remained at home for ten years until his mother's mourning was completed.

sentences.zh: 會子同書督貴州學政，陛辭，宣宗命傳諭促之來。

translations.literal: It happened that his son Tongshu was supervising educational administration in Guizhou; when taking leave at court, the Xuanzong Emperor ordered a message conveyed urging Xincun to come.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that his son Tongshu was serving as educational commissioner of Guizhou. When Tongshu took formal leave at court, Emperor Xuanzong ordered a message conveyed urging Xincun to return.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，至京，仍入直，授八阿哥讀。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he reached the capital, again entered regular service, and instructed the Eighth Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he reached the capital, resumed regular service, and was assigned to instruct the Eighth Prince.

sentences.zh: 補祭酒。

translations.literal: He was restored as libationer of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored to the post of libationer of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 歷內閣學士、工部侍郎，調戶部。

translations.literal: He served as Grand Secretariat academician, Vice Minister of Works, and was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served as grand secretariat academician and vice minister of works, then was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 江蘇巡撫請蘇州、松江、太倉漕米改徵折色，心存謂：「三屬額徵米一百十四萬餘石，一旦改折，慮京倉不敷支放，州縣假折色抑勒倍徵，便民適以累民。

translations.literal: The Jiangsu governor requested that tribute grain from Suzhou, Songjiang, and Taicang be converted to collection in commuted silver. Xincun said: "The three jurisdictions have a quota of more than 1,140,000 piculs of grain. If conversion is made all at once, I fear the capital granaries will lack sufficient disbursement, and prefectures and counties will use commuted silver as a pretext to extort double levies, turning convenience for the people into a burden on the people."
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangsu governor requested that tribute grain from Suzhou, Songjiang, and Taicang be collected in commuted silver instead. Xincun argued: "The three jurisdictions have a quota of more than 1,140,000 piculs of grain. If conversion is made all at once, I fear the capital granaries will lack sufficient grain for disbursement, and prefectures and counties will use commuted silver as a pretext to extort double levies, turning a measure meant to help the people into a burden on them."

sentences.zh: 」主駁議，事乃寢。

translations.literal: " He led the opposition, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: " He led the opposition, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xianfeng reign he was promoted to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 三年，江寧陷，心存疏陳兵事，請乘賊勢未定，飭向榮渡江，陳金綬進屯浦口，以上海水師溯流沖其前，江忠源、鄧紹良之師掩其後，四路進攻；

translations.literal: In the third year, when Jiangning fell, Xincun memorialized on military affairs, requesting that while the bandit strength was not yet settled, Xiang Rong be ordered to cross the river, Chen Jinshou advance and encamp at Pukou, the Shanghai naval force strike upstream at their front, and the armies of Jiang Zhongyuan and Deng Shaoliang fall upon their rear in a four-pronged attack;
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when Jiangning fell, Xincun memorialized on military affairs. He urged that while rebel strength was not yet consolidated, Xiang Rong be ordered to cross the Yangtze, Chen Jinshou advance and encamp at Pukou, the Shanghai naval force strike upstream at their front, and the armies of Jiang Zhongyuan and Deng Shaoliang fall upon their rear in a four-pronged attack;

sentences.zh: 增重兵守江、淮杜北竄；

translations.literal: heavy forces be added to guard the Yangtze and Huai and block northern flight;
translations.idiomatic: heavy forces be added to guard the Yangtze and Huai and block a northern breakout;

sentences.zh: 急清兗、豫、鳳、潁捻匪，毋令與粵寇合勢；

translations.literal: the Nian bandits in Yan, Yu, Feng, and Ying be quickly cleared so they do not join strength with the Guangdong rebels;
translations.idiomatic: the Nian bandits in Yan, Yu, Feng, and Ying be quickly suppressed so they do not join forces with the Guangdong rebels;

sentences.zh: 並覈軍需，卹災黎；

translations.literal: military supplies be audited and disaster victims relieved;
translations.idiomatic: military supplies be audited and disaster victims relieved;

sentences.zh: 籌京倉積貯，整飭紀綱，以維根本。

translations.literal: and capital granary stores be planned, discipline rectified, to preserve the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: and stores in the capital granaries be built up and discipline rectified in order to preserve the foundations of the state.

sentences.zh: 疏上，多被採用。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, much was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, many of his proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 又薦湖北按察使江忠源，請畀統帥重任，尋即擢為巡撫。

translations.literal: He also recommended Hubei provincial surveillance commissioner Jiang Zhongyuan, requesting that he be given heavy command responsibility, and soon he was promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended Hubei provincial surveillance commissioner Jiang Zhongyuan and asked that he be given major command responsibility. Jiang was soon promoted to governor.

sentences.zh: 調刑部，再調工部，兼管順天府尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Justice, then again to the Ministry of Works, and concurrently supervised the Shuntian prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of Justice, then back to the Ministry of Works, and was also put in charge of the Shuntian prefect.

sentences.zh: 粵匪北犯，心存疏言賊氛逼近，請扼河而守，畿南直駐重兵，河南、山西、陝西各要隘並力堵截，速調駐熱河、綏遠之蒙古馬隊進口內衛京畿；

translations.literal: When Guangdong bandits invaded northward, Xincun memorialized that the bandit threat was drawing near, requesting defense by holding the river line, heavy forces stationed directly south of the capital region, key passes in Henan, Shanxi, and Shaanxi jointly blocked, and Mongol cavalry stationed at Rehe and Suiyuan quickly transferred inside the passes to guard the capital region;
translations.idiomatic: When the Guangdong rebels invaded northward, Xincun memorialized that the rebel threat was drawing near. He urged holding the river line, stationing heavy forces directly south of the capital region, jointly blocking key passes in Henan, Shanxi, and Shaanxi, and quickly transferring Mongol cavalry stationed at Rehe and Suiyuan inside the passes to guard the capital region;

sentences.zh: 京師九門嚴緝姦宄，運通倉存糧入城；

translations.literal: the nine gates of the capital strictly hunt down traitors and spies, and grain stored at the Tongcang granary be transported into the city;
translations.idiomatic: the nine gates of the capital strictly hunt down traitors and spies, and grain stored at the Tongcang granary be transported into the city;

sentences.zh: 並敕琦善、鄧紹良規复揚州、鎮江，為會剿江寧之計。

translations.literal: and Qishan and Deng Shaoliang be ordered to plan recovery of Yangzhou and Zhenjiang as a step toward joint suppression at Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: and Qishan and Deng Shaoliang be ordered to plan the recovery of Yangzhou and Zhenjiang as a step toward a joint campaign against Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 又疏陳順天防務，畫分汛地，舉行團練；

translations.literal: He also memorialized on Shuntian defense, delineating garrison zones and organizing militia training;
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized on Shuntian defense, delineating garrison zones and organizing militia training;

sentences.zh: 府屬各營舊隸總督管轄，請旨暫歸調遣。

translations.literal: the various camps under the prefecture having formerly been under the governor's jurisdiction, he requested an edict that they temporarily be placed under his dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: the various camps under the prefecture having formerly been under the governor's jurisdiction, he requested an edict placing them temporarily under his command.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊犯天津，僧格林沁率師進剿，命順天府設糧台。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits threatened Tianjin; Sengge Rinchen led troops in pursuit, and Shuntian was ordered to establish a grain supply office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels threatened Tianjin. Sengge Rinchen led troops in pursuit, and Shuntian was ordered to establish a grain supply office.

sentences.zh: 心存請發內帑三十二萬兩、京倉米二千六百石以給軍食，添制軍需火藥。

translations.literal: Xincun requested disbursement of 320,000 taels from the inner treasury and 2,600 piculs of grain from the capital granary to supply the army, and additional manufacture of military gunpowder.
translations.idiomatic: Xincun requested disbursement of 320,000 taels from the inner treasury and 2,600 piculs of grain from the capital granary to supply the army, along with additional manufacture of military gunpowder.

sentences.zh: 又偕團防大臣會議京城防守事宜，舉光祿寺卿宋晉、太僕寺卿王茂廕綜理其事，並詔允行。

translations.literal: He also joined the militia defense ministers in conference on capital defense, recommending Court of Imperial Entertainments Director Song Jin and Court of the Imperial Stud Director Wang Maoyin to oversee the matter, and an edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined the militia defense ministers in conference on capital defense and recommended Court of Imperial Entertainments director Song Jin and Court of the Imperial Stud director Wang Maoyin to oversee the work. An edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 時議行鈔幣，心存疏言：「軍營搭放票鈔，諸多窒礙。

translations.literal: At the time there was discussion of issuing paper currency; Xincun memorialized: "Distributing paper notes in military camps involves many obstacles."
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was discussion of issuing paper currency. Xincun memorialized: "Distributing paper notes in military camps involves many obstacles."

sentences.zh: 鈔幣之法，施行當有次第，此時甫經頒發，並未試用，勢難驟用之軍營。

translations.literal: The method of paper currency should be implemented in proper sequence; it has only just been issued and not yet tried, and it will be difficult to apply it suddenly in military camps.
translations.idiomatic: The method of paper currency should be implemented in proper sequence. It has only just been issued and not yet tried, and it will be difficult to apply it suddenly in military camps.

sentences.zh: 」詔斥為阻撓，即責籌次等施行之法，俾無阻滯。

translations.literal: " An edict rebuked this as obstruction and immediately charged him to devise graded methods of implementation so there would be no hindrance.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict rebuked this as obstruction and immediately charged him to devise graded methods of implementation so there would be no delay.

sentences.zh: 會言官論通州捕役勾結土匪行劫，命刑部侍郎文瑞鞫得實，心存以徇庇革職。

translations.literal: It happened that censors discussed Tongzhou constables colluding with bandits to commit robbery; Vice Minister of Justice Wen Rui was ordered to investigate and found the charges true; Xincun was stripped of office for favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that censors reported Tongzhou constables colluding with bandits to commit robbery. Vice Minister of Justice Wen Rui was ordered to investigate and found the charges true. Xincun was stripped of office for showing favoritism.

sentences.zh: 四年，起授吏部侍郎，調戶部，擢兵部尚書，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was recalled and appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, transferred to Revenue, promoted to Minister of War, and transferred to Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was recalled and appointed vice minister of personnel, transferred to the Ministry of Revenue, promoted to minister of war, and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 六年，疏陳江南軍事，略曰：「蘇、松、常、太三府一州，及浙之杭、嘉、湖三府，久為賊所窺伺。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he memorialized on Jiangnan military affairs, stating in summary: "The three prefectures and one department of Su, Song, Chang, and Tai, and the three prefectures of Hang, Jia, and Hu in Zhejiang, have long been watched by the bandits."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he memorialized on Jiangnan military affairs, writing in summary: "The three prefectures and one department of Su, Song, Chang, and Tai, and the three prefectures of Hang, Jia, and Hu in Zhejiang, have long been eyed by the rebels."

sentences.zh: 今寧國先陷，逼近宜興，向榮近守丹陽，溧水、句容相繼失守，宜責向榮嚴扼丹陽，令張國樑率精兵駐宜興扼東壩，別簡水師駐太湖，庶蘇、常兩郡可保無事。

translations.literal: Now Ningguo has fallen first and draws near Yixing; Xiang Rong recently guards Danyang; Lishui and Jurong have successively been lost. Xiang Rong should be charged strictly to hold Danyang, Zhang Guoliang ordered to lead elite troops to encamp at Yixing and hold Dongba, and a separate naval force selected to station at Taihu, so that the two prefectures of Su and Chang may be kept secure.
translations.idiomatic: Now Ningguo has fallen and the threat draws near Yixing. Xiang Rong is holding Danyang, but Lishui and Jurong have fallen in succession. Xiang Rong should be ordered strictly to hold Danyang, Zhang Guoliang should lead elite troops to encamp at Yixing and hold Dongba, and a separate naval force should be stationed on Lake Tai, so that the prefectures of Suzhou and Changzhou may be kept secure.

sentences.zh: 又近有按畝捐輸，失政體，竭民財，請查明停止。

translations.literal: Moreover, there has recently been donation by the mu; this violates proper governance, exhausts the people's wealth, and I request investigation and cessation.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, there has recently been per-mu donation levies, which violate proper governance, exhaust the people's wealth, and should be investigated and halted.

sentences.zh: 」是年冬，兼翰林院掌院學士，以吏部尚書協辦大學士，尋調戶部。

translations.literal: " That winter he concurrently served as Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, and as Minister of Personnel was appointed Associate Grand Secretary; soon he was transferred to Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: " That winter he was also made chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and, as minister of personnel, was appointed associate grand secretary. Soon afterward he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 八年，充上書房總師傅。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed chief tutor of the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed chief tutor of the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 英法聯軍北犯，天津戒嚴。

translations.literal: The Anglo-French allied armies invaded northward and Tianjin was placed under martial law.
translations.idiomatic: The Anglo-French allied armies invaded northward and Tianjin was placed under martial law.

sentences.zh: 心存疏請聖駕還宮，以定眾志，力言京師重地，不可駐外國領事；

translations.literal: Xincun memorialized requesting the sacred carriage return to the palace to settle popular resolve, forcefully stating that the capital was a vital place where foreign consuls must not be stationed;
translations.idiomatic: Xincun memorialized asking that the imperial procession return to the palace to steady public resolve. He forcefully argued that the capital was too vital a place to station foreign consuls;

sentences.zh: 長江形勢不可失；

translations.literal: the strategic position of the Yangtze must not be lost;
translations.idiomatic: the strategic position of the Yangtze must not be lost;

sentences.zh: 綏芬邊地不可捐；

translations.literal: the Suifen borderlands must not be surrendered;
translations.idiomatic: the Suifen borderlands must not be surrendered;

sentences.zh: 兵費不可再償；

translations.literal: military expenses must not be paid again;
translations.idiomatic: war indemnities must not be paid again;

sentences.zh: 傳教不可推廣；

translations.literal: missionary activity must not be expanded;
translations.idiomatic: missionary activity must not be expanded;

sentences.zh: 和議難成，宜速進剿。

translations.literal: peace talks will be hard to conclude, and rapid advance in suppression is appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: peace talks will be hard to conclude, and a rapid advance in suppression is appropriate.

sentences.zh: 湖北巡撫胡林翼奏除漕務中飽之弊，請改徵折色。

translations.literal: Hubei Governor Hu Linyi memorialized to eliminate the abuses of graft in tribute transport affairs and requested conversion to commuted silver collection.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei governor Hu Linyi memorialized to eliminate graft in tribute transport affairs and requested conversion to commuted silver collection.

sentences.zh: 心存力贊其議；

translations.literal: Xincun strongly endorsed his proposal;
translations.idiomatic: Xincun strongly endorsed his proposal;

sentences.zh: 由部定章程五事，滿、漢兵糧折價支給，上下衙門一切陋規概行裁革焉。

translations.literal: the ministry fixed regulations in five articles, Manchu and Han military grain rations paid at converted prices, and all corrupt practices in upper and lower offices were in general abolished.
translations.idiomatic: the ministry fixed regulations in five articles, Manchu and Han military grain rations were paid at converted prices, and corrupt practices throughout the bureaucracy were in general abolished.

sentences.zh: 拜體仁閣大學士，管理戶部。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Embodying Benevolence and supervised the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand secretary of the Hall of Embodying Benevolence and put in charge of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 與肅順同官不相能，屢乞病，不許。

translations.literal: Serving in the same office as Sushun, he could not get along with him and repeatedly pleaded illness to retire, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Serving in the same office as Sushun, he could not get along with him and repeatedly pleaded illness to retire, but was not permitted.
